01.r: Marks Levi as the one exception in the share-out of the land.
01.n: The brief's lexicon lists 'save, except (after a negative)' among its senses.

02.r: Levi as a tribe among the tribes.
02.n: BDB: rod, staff, club, sceptre; tribe.

03.r: The tribe set apart for the sanctuary.
03.n: The Hebrew has the article, literally 'the tribe of the Levite', the tribe named by its members.

05.r: When the land was shared out, Levi was given none.
05.n: The subject is not named; the BSB supplies 'Moses'. That Moses is meant is a reasonable reading of the surrounding account, which the brief does not show.

06.n: Gesenius notes this noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe.

07.r: The sacrifices given to the LORD on the altar, from which the priests take their share.
07.n: Gesenius: a sacrifice, so called from the fire by which it is burned. The KJV, Geneva and DRC say 'sacrifices'.
t: the sacrifices of ... made by fire
the offerings of ... made by fire
the offerings of ... made by fire

08.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

09.r: Names the LORD as Israel's own God.

11.r: Points back to the fire offerings and names them as the inheritance.
11.n: The pronoun 'he, it' used as 'that': there is no verb in the Hebrew. The translations turn it into 'are'.

12.r: What a tribe would hold as land, Levi holds in the offerings.
12.n: 'Its' is the tribe, singular in Hebrew; the KJV and BSB say 'their', the Geneva, DRC, JPS and ASV 'his'.

13.r: Points back to what the LORD had already said.

14.r: The LORD's earlier word to Levi.
14.n: The verb is 'speak'; the brief's lexicon lists 'to promise' among its senses in this form, which is how the BSB takes it.

05.n: ἐδόθη, 'was given', a passive where the Hebrew has 'he gave'.

08.n: The Greek has nothing for 'the fire offerings of': it reads 'the Lord God of Israel, he is their inheritance', making the LORD himself the inheritance.

14.n: εἶπεν, 'he said'. The brief gives no dictionary form; εἶπεν is from εἶπον.
